title: For the Love of Fire
description: 161123-N-PA426-001 PEARL HARBOR  (Nov. 23, 2016) Petty Officer 2nd Class Michael Edwards stationed at Surface Warfare Officers School (SWOS), Engineering Learning Site Pearl Harbor, talks about being a Damage Controlman. Edwards instructs Sailors in general shipboard firefighting training. The training allowed students to practice proper hose handling procedures, fire fighting maneuvers, teamwork and nozzle man relieving procedures. (U.S. Navy video by Petty Officer 1st Class Meranda Keller/Released)

transcript.text: - [Voiceover] There is no greater threat to a deployed Navy
vessel than a fire onboard.
Without the possibility of outside help
or at a chance at an evacuation,
sailors must be prepared to deal with a fire
should one occur.
- [Voiceover] Petty Officer Michael Edwards
learned early in his career
how quickly a dangerous situation can arise.
- My scariest day on the job would have to be
'bout 02:00 just on deployment,
and hearing the actual word,
like, "Major fuel oil leak
in the machinery room," which we are trained
like, that is the worst possible thing that can happen.
Especially on a deployment,
in the middle of nowhere where there is no 911.
I am 911.
- [Voiceover] Edwards doesn't shrink from the pressure.
In fact, he sought it out.
- [Edwards] This Is my dream journey.
From the time I went into the fleet
and I went to my first Firefighting school,
I went through the course and I was like,
"This is what I want to do. I wanna do what they do,
those people in the red coveralls."
- [Voiceover] Edwards did just that.
He now wears those coveralls
for Surface Warfare Officers School
at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam
where he trains other sailors to fight fire.
- [Edwards] The first trainer was the Aviation fire.
The team comes in here and they practice movements.
It also allows them to practice communications
before they go into the main machinery fire,
which is, oh my gosh, is the worst thing
that can happen on the ship.
And they are wearing all their gear.
Typically, that fire is a lot worse
because it's ran off of fuel.
And fuel is what makes the ship go and it's everywhere.
- [Voiceover] Edwards takes pride in improving the safety
of Navy vessels, and improving the sailors who work on them.
- [Edwards] My favorite part of the job
would have to be actually getting in there,
the fire and training the students.
And having the students come back to me and say,
"You taught me a lot."
- [Voiceover] I'm Petty Officer Miranda Keller,
Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
